tagline: Over the mountains slow on 71, back fast through the tunnel.
intro: From Dean's Market at the edge of the Arkansas River Valley two roads cross the Boston Mountains to Fayetteville, and together they make a loop. Old US 71 takes 42 miles, winding through the small towns the interstate passes by. I-49 does it in 38, on high bridges through rugged country, with views over oak-hickory mountains and small farms in the valleys.

The Butterfield Overland Mail ran its stagecoaches over these mountains, and US 71 took their place in 1926. Old 71 was once classed among the most dangerous highways in America, and I-49, finished in 1999, was built to make the trip safer.

moments.title: Mountainburg
moments.text: A railroad town of 1883 that did well while 71 was the main road and has been sleepier since the interstate, keeping two large dinosaur models in its downtown park since 1980.

moments.title: Winslow
moments.text: A stagecoach stop first called Summit Home, renamed for the Frisco's president in 1881, and by the end of the 1800s a summer place for well-off families up from Fort Smith.

moments.title: Bobby Hopper Tunnel
moments.text: Coming back south on I-49 the road climbs inside twin bores of nearly 1,600 feet each through an unnamed peak, the only highway tunnel in Arkansas.
